ruling.reasoning:
The dispute is a route deviation on a completed RydeX trip. The trace settles RD-1: one off-route segment exists, 14:19–14:26, 5.03 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.39 km, +3.64 km, up to 1160 m off the optimal route [F3][RD-1]. Nothing exempts it: no traffic incident on the replaced stretch (F11 shows none; the Ayer Rajah and Central Expressway speed bands 4 are only corroborative and cannot exempt alone) [F9][F10][F11][RD-4], no rider message on record before 14:19 [F7], and the driver's post-trip statement "The GPS rerouted me" is a claim, not rider consent [F8][RD-5].

The rider's own message confirms the fare was a fixed quote for RydeX, not a meter, and the fare record agrees: billed distance 10.68 km does not exceed the optimal 10.7 km, and the whole fare is base $3.90 + distance $15.06 + time $4.50 + platform $1.47 = $24.93, i.e. exactly the quoted basis with no additional charge tied to the extra 3.64 km and no unpublished item [F1][F4][F5][F6][RD-2]. On a non-metered service the policy refunds only ERP/toll and unpublished add-ons on the unexempt segment; there are none here, so the refundable amount is $0 [F6][RD-2][FARE-1]. Per RD-2 that yields no_action while still recording the RD-1 breach [F3][RD-2].

The driver was already given one upheld route dispute in the last 90 days (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2), and this case adds another established route violation, so RD-6 is triggered and the driver's account goes to Ryde account review; the profile alone is not the basis of the route finding, only of the flag [F14][RD-6][F3].

Safety screen: the only message-like material is the driver's post-trip statement "The GPS rerouted me, that's all. Nothing wrong with the fare." and the rider's complaint about the route and fare; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and F7 records no in-app chat at all [F7][F8][SAFE-1]. The record is sufficient to decide the whole dispute and the fixed-fare rule needs no further evidence [F4][F6][RD-2].

segment_findings.reason: No rider (or any) in-app chat message exists before the segment start 14:19:10 — the record has no chat at all [F7] — and the driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted him is a claim made after the detour began, which cannot establish the rider's consent [F8]. The segment therefore counts as a refundable detour under RD-2, subject to the deduction that this is a non-metered fare [RD-2][RD-5].
